classification.difficultyReason: Construct a nested absolute-value graph and determine parameter intervals from changes in its intersections with a straight line.

content.prompt:
Let $y=\left||x|-1\right|+k$ and $y=\dfrac{x}{2}-1$.

For what value(s) of $k$ will the number of intersection points be

inlines.text: The line passes through the right minimum; this is the only intersection.

answer.worked:
The intersections satisfy $h(x)=-k$, where $h(x)=\left||x|-1\right|-\dfrac{x}{2}+1$. Its corners are $(-1,\tfrac32)$, $(0,2)$ and $(1,\tfrac12)$, and both outer branches rise without bound. The horizontal line meets the graph once only at its global minimum, $(1,\tfrac12)$.
$$\begin{align*}-k&=\frac12\\k&=-\frac12\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Count two crossings between the critical levels or above the central maximum of the transformed graph.

answer.worked:
Count intersections of $y=h(x)$ and $y=-k$, where $h(x)=\left||x|-1\right|-\dfrac{x}{2}+1$. The corner heights are $\tfrac32$, $2$ and $\tfrac12$. There are two intersections when $\tfrac12<-k<\tfrac32$, or when $-k>2$. At the boundary levels the number changes.
$$-\frac32<k<-\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad k<-2.$$

inlines.text: At either boundary, two crossings merge into one at a corner.

answer.worked:
Use $h(x)=\left||x|-1\right|-\dfrac{x}{2}+1$ and count intersections with $y=-k$. At height $\tfrac32$, the horizontal line passes through the left minimum and crosses two other branches. At height $2$, it passes through the central maximum and crosses both outer branches. Each gives three distinct intersections.
$$k=-\frac32\quad\text{or}\quad k=-2.$$

inlines.text: The horizontal level crosses all four branches of the transformed graph.

answer.worked:
For $h(x)=\left||x|-1\right|-\dfrac{x}{2}+1$, a horizontal line crosses all four branches precisely between the left minimum, of height $\tfrac32$, and the central maximum, of height $2$.
$$\frac32<-k<2.$$
Therefore $-2<k<-\tfrac32$.

spec.description: Piecewise-linear graph h(x)=||x|-1|-x/2+1, with corners (-1,3/2), (0,2), (1,1/2). Dashed red horizontal guides show the three critical levels for intersections with y=-k.
spec.mathematics: h(x)=-3x/2 for x<=-1; h(x)=x/2+2 for -1<=x<=0; h(x)=2-3x/2 for 0<=x<=1; h(x)=x/2 for x>=1. The original intersections correspond exactly to h(x)=-k.
